History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
54-year-old male with hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with 2-hour history of sudden-onset central chest pressure (7/10) while gardening, associated with shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea, and left shoulder/arm pain. EMS activation arranged for possible acute cardiac event.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Central chest pressure (“like someone sitting on my chest”).  
• Onset/duration: Sudden onset while gardening; ongoing for “a couple of hours,” unchanged in intensity.  
• Severity: 7/10 initially and currently.  
• Character: Pressure/discomfort rather than sharp pain.  
• Radiation: To left shoulder and arm; no radiation to head or back.  
• Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting), exertional dyspnea on stairs/hills (recent), calf pain and leg swelling, no dysphagia, no urinary/bowel issues.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None reported; persists at rest.  
• Review of systems: No other chest pain descriptors provided; no swallowing difficulty, no reported palpitations, syncope, cough, fever, abdominal pain.

Past Medical History:
• Hypertension – untreated.  
• Hypercholesterolemia – untreated.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• No regular medications.  
Allergies:
• Not documented.

Social History:
• Smokes (quantity/frequency not documented).  
• Lives with wife at home.  
• Gardening every other week; recently limiting activity due to exertional dyspnea.  
• Alcohol and other substance use not discussed.

Family History:
• Not mentioned.

Physical Examination:
• No physical examination or vitals documented (remote consult pending EMS arrival).

Investigations:
• None performed prior to EMS arrival.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Chest discomfort with concerning features (pressure, SOB, left arm radiation) in patient with HTN and hyperlipidemia. Possible acute coronary syndrome.  
  – Plan: Activate emergency services; patient instructed to await ambulance with wife present.  
  – Advise to remain calm, sip water as needed, no medications until assessed.  
  – Paramedics to obtain vitals, ECG, cardiac enzymes as per protocol.  
  – ED evaluation by cardiology/medical team on arrival.  

Issue 2: Exertional dyspnea with calf pain/leg swelling – consider precipitating cardiac ischemia or alternative pathology (e.g., heart failure, pulmonary embolism).  
  – Plan: Flag for EMS/ED team; further assessment with physical exam, imaging (CXR, possible lower-limb ultrasound, CT pulmonary angiography if indicated).  

Issue 3: Untreated hypertension and hyperlipidemia.  
  – Plan: After acute episode, arrange primary care follow-up for cardiovascular risk modification, medication initiation, and lifestyle counseling.  

General Plan items:  
  – Babylon physician to schedule follow-up telehealth appointment after hospital evaluation.  
  – Documentation to accompany patient via EMS; consultant to provide update to telehealth physician.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: No allergy information, no medication reconciliation details, no vitals, no objective exam findings.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional conversational overlap but clinically adequate.
